card: Exposes Bitcoin Core's Chain interface over IPC using Cap'n Proto proxy wrappers, dividing it into a version-stable Chain interface for external clients and an UnstableChain interface for internal consumers. Currently, IPC clients can access mining and RPC interfaces but cannot query chain state or receive chain events, blocking out-of-process wallet execution (#10102). The split allows external clients stable block lookup methods while preserving the flexibility to refactor internal wallet APIs across releases. This change is a prerequisite for running bitcoin-wallet as a separate process (#19460) and depends on #36520.
changed_since_previous: Includes documentation fixes for findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight and FoundBlock::locator comments addressing review feedback, and rebases on an updated libmultiprocess subtree commit.
evidence: PR description: 'Processes connected to bitcoin-node over IPC (with -ipcbind) can use the Mining interface, but they can't currently use the Chain interface to read chain data or follow chain events. Chain data could be useful to third-party clients and Bitcoin Core's own wallet could use this as well to run in a separate process (#10102).'

PR description notes that without interface separation, 'exposing all of interfaces::Chain to external clients would make its methods hard to change, since the wallet uses them as internal API (#34981).'
problem: Processes connected to bitcoin-node over IPC cannot query chain data or listen to chain notifications, preventing bitcoin-wallet from running in a separate process (#10102). Exposing all of interfaces::Chain directly as an external API would freeze internal wallet methods against future refactoring (#34981).

risk.why: Flaws in IPC serialization or proxy wrappers could cause node crashes or miscommunicate chain state to IPC clients such as external tools or a detached wallet process.

scope_notes: Carries an update to the src/ipc/libmultiprocess subtree as its first commit and adds extensive Cap'n Proto serialization boilerplate in src/ipc/capnp/chain.cpp.
summary: Exposes the node's interfaces::Chain over IPC using Cap'n Proto proxy wrappers, divided into a version-stable Chain interface and an UnstableChain interface. The stable interface provides basic block lookup methods with backward-compatibility guarantees for external clients, while UnstableChain exposes all remaining methods for internal consumers like bitcoin-wallet. The change also adds serialization helpers for common Bitcoin Core types, adjusts several interfaces::Chain signatures to support code generation, and updates the libmultiprocess subtree.
